Now let me sample the actual background regions of frame 1 using sharp, since the subject-safe sampling assumption I made earlier doesn't tell me where the vault sits within frame 1. I'll grab the frame dimensions plus samples from the four corners and the viewport center, all using the real frame's aspect ratio, so the page gradient is built from the real background tones rather than the vault body.
The issue is a JSON parse error in the call — the string has to be valid JSON itself. I'll fix the sampling command to use a clean single-line script without embedded newlines, then run it so I have the color samples the spec requires before implementing the hero.

## Result

The clip canvas is rendered by `HeroVault` inside `.hero-stage` — the element `hero-timeline` applies pointer parallax to, whose parent `.hero-stage-wrap` carries the float, so both canvases move together and the float is untouched. ## Blocker to report — mobile CTAs are unreachable

At <1024 px the CTAs sit below the fold (Sign up at y≈974 on a 900 px viewport), so reaching them requires scrolling. `hero-timeline`'s scroll handoff fades `.hero-copy` and sets `pointer-events: none` at ~55 px of scroll, at **every** width. Measured at 375: scroll 40 → copy opacity 0.26; scroll 100 → opacity 0, `pointer-events: none`, hit test resolves to `.hero-shell`. So on a real phone the Sign up button cannot be hovered or tapped at all — a v1 defect, not something this clip introduced.

{"kind":"tool","id":"a1eu2IYgZ0g","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/VaultSequence.tsx","instructions":"Remove the sequence canvas, its preload and draw loop; keep the pinned captions.","content":"// VaultSequence.tsx — pinned escrow narrative scrubbed by the scroll.
// The section pins for ~3.6 viewports while six caption scenes cross-fade on
// scroll progress. Reduced motion falls back to two static frames + stacked
// captions. (The frame-sequence canvas was removed; captions are the only
// scrubbed content left.)
import { useRef, useEffect, useCallback } from "react";
import gsap from "gsap";
import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger";
import Lenis from "lenis";
import { StateToken } from "./StateToken";
import { ArrowRight } from "./icons";
import { PrimaryButton } from "./VaultButtons";

gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);
ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true });

const FRAME_COUNT = 120;

/** Frame source — first frame is public/vault-frames/f_001.webp, last is f_120.webp.
 *  Only the reduced-motion fallback still reads frames (two stills).
 *  The small 960px set lives at /public/vault-frames-sm/ and exists (120 files).
 */
const FRAME_SRC = (i: number, sm: boolean) =>
  `${
    sm ? "/vault-frames-sm" : "/vault-frames"
  }/f_${String(i + 1).padStart(3, "0")}.webp`;

const clamp01 = (x: number) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x));

const SCENES: Array<{
  from: number;
  to: number;
  head: string;
  sub: string;
  cta?: boolean;
}> = [
  { from: 0,  to: 20,  head: "The vault is sealed.", sub: "Twenty sealed frames load before the scroll ever moves. No motion until the assets are ready." },
  { from: 20, to: 45,  head: "Pressure builds inside.", sub: "The mechanism turns while the vault stays shut. Every frame is a frame of the same locked state." },
  { from: 45, to: 70,  head: "The lock interrogates.", sub: "The work is checked while it is still sealed. No output before a verdict." },
  { from: 70, to: 90,  head: "The mechanism opens.", sub: "On a clear verdict, the vault breaks apart. The files emerge in the open." },
  { from: 90, to: 105, head: "Capture releases the payment.", sub: "Only a captured payment unlocks the work. A rejected verdict voids the hold — nothing moves." },
  { from: 105, to: 119, head: "Walk the whole handshake.", sub: "See the full escrow life in one continuous scroll, then put it to the test in the sandbox.", cta: true },
];

type SceneDef = (typeof SCENES)[number];

export function VaultSequence() {
  const sectionRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const pinRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const lenisRef = useRef<Lenis | null>(null);
  const reducedMotion = useRef(
    typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches
  );
  const pinEnd = useRef("+=350%");

  // resolve responsive config once, on mount, client-side only
  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
    pinEnd.current = window.innerWidth < 768 ? "+=250%" : "+=350%";
  }, []);

  // Lenis + the pin that holds the section while the captions scrub
  useEffect(() => {
    if (reducedMotion.current) return;
    const pin = pinRef.current;
    const section = sectionRef.current;
    if (!pin || !section) return;

    const lenis = new Lenis({
      duration: 1.2,
      easing: (t) => Math.min(1, 1.001 - Math.pow(2, -10 * t)),
      smoothWheel: true,
    });
    lenisRef.current = lenis;

    // Lenis drives its own RAF loop (autoRaf on by default). ScrollTrigger
    // refreshes on Lenis scroll, and gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0) keeps the
    // scrub synced to the real scroll delta rather than an interpolated ticker.
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
    lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update as any);

    const trigger = ScrollTrigger.create({
      trigger: section,
      start: "top top",
      end: pinEnd.current,
      pin,
      pinSpacing: true,
      anticipatePin: 1,
      invalidateOnRefresh: true,
    });

    return () => {
      trigger.kill();
      lenis.destroy();
      lenisRef.current = null;
    };
  }, []);

  // caption scene visibility — a scrub proxy driven by the same end point
  const progress = useRef(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (reducedMotion.current || !sectionRef.current) return;
    const proxy = { v: 0 };
    const animation = gsap.to(proxy, {
      v: 1,
      ease: "none",
      scrollTrigger: {
        trigger: sectionRef.current,
        start: "top top",
        end: pinEnd.current,
        scrub: 0.5,
        onUpdate: () => {
          progress.current = proxy.v;
        },
      },
    });
    return () => {
      animation.scrollTrigger?.kill();
      animation.kill();
    };
  }, []);

  const sceneOpacity = useCallback(
    (scene: SceneDef) => {
      const p = reducedMotion.current ? 0 : progress.current;
      const inRamp = clamp01((p - scene.from / (FRAME_COUNT - 1)) / 0.05);
      const outRamp = clamp01((p - scene.to / (FRAME_COUNT - 1)) / 0.05);
      return Math.min(inRamp, 1 - outRamp);
    },
    []
  );

  const captionY = useCallback(
    (scene: SceneDef) => {
      const p = reducedMotion.current ? 0 : progress.current;
      const inRamp = clamp01((p - scene.from / (FRAME_COUNT - 1)) / 0.05);
      const outRamp = clamp01((p - scene.to / (FRAME_COUNT - 1)) / 0.05);
      return (1 - inRamp) * 16 - outRamp * 12;
    },
    []
  );

  // reduced-motion fallback — no pin, two static frames with the captions
  // stacked below them.
  if (reducedMotion.current) {
    return (
      <section
        className="vs"
        ref={sectionRef}
        aria-label="VaultPay escrow sequence — reduced-motion fallback"
        data-testid="vault-sequence"
      >
        <div className="vs-fallback-stack">
          <div className="vs-fallback-frames">
            <img
              src={FRAME_SRC(0, true)}
              alt="Vault closed — frame 1 of the escrow sequence"
              className="vs-frame is-ready"
              decoding="async"
              loading="eager"
            />
            <img
              src={FRAME_SRC(FRAME_COUNT - 1, true)}
              alt="Vault exploded view — frame 120 of the escrow sequence"
              className="vs-frame is-ready"
              decoding="async"
              loading="eager"
            />
          </div>
          <div className="vs-copy vs-copy-static">
            {SCENES.map((s) => (
              <div key={s.head} className="vs-scene vs-scene-static">
                <div className="vs-scene-inner">
                  <StateToken
                    state={stateTokenForHead(s.head)}
                  />
                  <h2 className="vs-head">{s.head}</h2>
                  <p className="small vs-sub">{s.sub}</p>
                  {s.cta && (
                    <PrimaryButton onClick={() => {}}>
                      Put it to Test <ArrowRight />
                    </PrimaryButton>
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      </section>
    );
  }

  // normal motion — pinned captions, no frame canvas
  return (
    <section
      className="vs"
      ref={sectionRef}
      aria-label="VaultPay escrow sequence"
      data-testid="vault-sequence"
    >
      <div className="vs-pin" ref={pinRef} style={{ position: "relative" }}>
        <div className="vs-copy" aria-live="polite">
          {SCENES.map((s) => {
            const op = sceneOpacity(s);
            const y = captionY(s);
            const visible = op > 0.025;
            return (
              <div
                key={s.head}
                className="vs-scene"
                style={{
                  opacity: op,
                  visibility: visible ? "visible" : "hidden",
                  transform: `translateY(${y.toFixed(2)}px)`,
                }}
              >
                <div className="vs-scene-inner">
                  <StateToken
                    state={stateTokenForHead(s.head)}
                  />
                  <h2 className="vs-head">{s.head}</h2>
                  <p className="small vs-sub">{s.sub}</p>
                  {s.cta && (
                    <div className="vs-cta">
                      <PrimaryButton onClick={() => {}}>
                        Put it to Test <ArrowRight />
                      </PrimaryButton>
                      <p className="ticker-note">
                        60 seconds. No signup. Sandbox means no money moves.
                      </p>
                    </div>
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
            );
          })}
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

// Map caption heads to the app's lifecycle state tokens, matching the existing
// VaultScroll narrative so the sequence reads as the same escrow story.
function stateTokenForHead(head: string): "SEALED" | "HELD" | "AUDITING" | "CAPTURED" | "PAID" {
  if (head.includes("sealed")) return "SEALED";
  if (head.includes("pressure")) return "HELD";
  if (head.includes("interrogates")) return "AUDITING";
  if (head.includes("opens") || head.includes("payment")) return "CAPTURED";
  return "PAID";
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"a5NWvYDsoD0","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"scripts/gen-clip-manifest.mjs","instructions":"Generate the keypad clip manifest from the frames folder.","content":"/* gen-clip-manifest.mjs — the browser cannot list public/ at runtime, so the
   keypad clip URLs are generated here. Files are sorted numerically and URL
   encoded once (the folder name contains a space). */

import { readdirSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { resolve, dirname, join } from "node:path";

const SOURCE_DIR = "public/Keypad frames";
const OUT_FILE = "src/config/keypad-manifest.json";
const PATTERN = /^ezgif-frame-(\d+)\.webp$/i;

const frameNumber = (name) => Number(name.match(PATTERN)[1]);

const urls = [];
if (existsSync(SOURCE_DIR)) {
  const files = readdirSync(SOURCE_DIR)
    .filter((name) => PATTERN.test(name))
    .sort((a, b) => frameNumber(a) - frameNumber(b));
  const folder = "/" + encodeURIComponent(SOURCE_DIR.replace(/^public\//, "").replace(/\\/g, "/"));
  for (const name of files) urls.push(`${folder}/${encodeURIComponent(name)}`);
} else {
  console.warn(`[gen-clip-manifest] ${SOURCE_DIR} not found — writing an empty manifest`);
}

mkdirSync(dirname(OUT_FILE), { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(OUT_FILE, JSON.stringify(urls, null, 2) + "\n");
console.log(`[gen-clip-manifest] ${urls.length} keypad frames -> ${OUT_FILE}`);
"}}

{"kind":"tool","id":"a5-gud73MF0","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"scripts/verify-keypad-2.mjs","instructions":"Check keypad reverse, canvas exclusivity and the unchanged wheel clip.","content":"import { chromium } from "playwright";

const b = await chromium.launch();
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
await p.goto("http://127.0.0.1:5173/", { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
await p.waitForTimeout(9000);

const read = () => p.evaluate(() => {
  const one = (sel) => {
    const c = document.querySelector(sel);
    const d = c.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height).data;
    let alpha = 0;
    for (let i = 3; i < d.length; i += 4 * 97) if (d[i] > 8) alpha++;
    return { alpha, op: Number(getComputedStyle(c).opacity) };
  };
  const still = document.querySelector("canvas.hero-canvas:not(.hero-clip)");
  const sd = still.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, still.width, still.height).data;
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < sd.length; i += 4 * 101) h = (h * 33 + sd[i] + sd[i + 1] * 5) % 1000000007;
  return {
    pad: one('[data-testid="keypad-clip"]'),
    wheel: one('[data-testid="wheel-clip"]'),
    still: h,
    keypadDom: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(".hero-keypad")).visibility,
  };
});

const before = await read();
await p.hover('[data-testid="hero-signin"]');
await p.waitForTimeout(1000);
const mid = await read();
await p.mouse.move(1400, 40);
const t0 = Date.now();
let cleared = -1;
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  const s = await read();
  if (s.pad.op === 0 && s.pad.alpha === 0) { cleared = Date.now() - t0; break; }
  await p.waitForTimeout(100);
}
const after = await read();
console.log("reverse", JSON.stringify({ before, mid, clearedMs: cleared, after }));

/* exclusivity: Sign up then Sign in immediately */
await p.hover('[data-testid="hero-signup"]');
await p.waitForTimeout(400);
await p.hover('[data-testid="hero-signin"]');
let overlap = 0;
const seen = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  const s = await read();
  if (s.pad.alpha > 0 && s.wheel.alpha > 0) overlap++;
  if (i % 10 === 0) seen.push(`w:${s.wheel.alpha}/p:${s.pad.alpha}`);
  await p.waitForTimeout(25);
}
console.log("exclusivity", JSON.stringify({ overlapSamples: overlap, seen }));

/* back to Sign up: wheel still behaves */
await p.mouse.move(1400, 40);
await p.waitForTimeout(4500);
await p.hover('[data-testid="hero-signup"]');
await p.waitForTimeout(1200);
console.log("wheel hover", JSON.stringify(await read()));
const t = Date.now();
await p.click('[data-testid="hero-signup"]');
await p.waitForURL("**/signup", { timeout: 6000 }).catch(() => {});
console.log("wheel click nav", Date.now() - t, "ms ->", p.url());

await b.close();
"}}

import { chromium } from "playwright";
import fs from "node:fs";

const URL = "http://127.0.0.1:5173/";
const OUT = "docs/hero-shots/intro";
fs.mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });

const opacity = (sel) => `Number(document.querySelector('${sel}').style.opacity || 0)`;

const browser = await chromium.launch();
const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
const page = await ctx.newPage();
await page.goto(URL, { waitUntil: "load" });

const waitFor = async (sel, min, timeout) => {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  while (Date.now() - t0 < timeout) {
    if ((await page.evaluate(opacity(sel))) >= min) return true;
    await page.waitForTimeout(100);
  }
  return false;
};

const keypad = '[data-testid="keypad-clip"]';
const wheel = '[data-testid="wheel-clip"]';

const lit = await waitFor(keypad, 0.95, 15_000);
await page.waitForTimeout(900);
await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/01-keypad-lit.png` });

const turning = await waitFor(wheel, 0.95, 15_000);
await page.waitForTimeout(1_100);
await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/02-wheel-mid.png` });
await page.waitForTimeout(2_200);
await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/03-wheel-open.png` });

/* wait for the intro to finish: the wheel fades back out */
const t0 = Date.now();
while (Date.now() - t0 < 20_000) {
  if ((await page.evaluate(opacity(wheel))) < 0.02) break;
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
}
await page.waitForTimeout(500);
await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/04-rest.png` });

console.log(`keypad lit: ${lit}, wheel turned: ${turning}`);

await browser.close();
"}}

The first-visit intro is live: the vault lights its keypad, then turns the wheel once, then settles back to rest — and hover behaves exactly as before.

## What runs, and when

Once per browser (key `vaultpay.hero-intro.v1` in `localStorage`), on the first load only:

| t (from page load) | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 0 → 2.6s | existing entrance, untouched |
| ~3.3s | keypad clip fades in and the keys light in sequence (96 frames, plays to K1 = frame 48) |
| ~5.4s | keys hold lit for 618ms |
| ~6.0s | wheel clip takes the vault: one full turn, 81 frames (3.375s) |
| ~9.4s | wheel reverses back to the closed frame (3.375s), then fades out |
| ~13.2s | vault back at rest, seams and static frame restored |

The keypad plays to the **hover** amount, not the click amount — no code typing, no LED change, no navigation. The wheel runs exactly once, then closes itself so the very next hover starts from the same frame a fresh page would.

Two files changed:

- [HeroButtons.tsx](src/components/HeroButtons.tsx) — the intro runner, the arrival hooks it paces itself on, and the first-visit gate.
- [clipPlayer.ts](src/lib/clipPlayer.ts#L329) — one new `seek(frame)` so the keypad can be put back to rest instantly after the wheel cuts it (without it, the first Sign in hover would start with the keys already lit).

New harnesses: [intro-check.mjs](scripts/intro-check.mjs) and [intro-shots.mjs](scripts/intro-shots.mjs).

![Keypad lit, 1440](docs/hero-shots/intro/_preview/01-keypad-lit.png)

![Wheel turning, 1440](docs/hero-shots/intro/_preview/02-wheel-mid.png)

Browser-sampled, not inferred — I hashed the pixels on each clip canvas every 500ms so I could prove the frames actually advanced, not just that a canvas got opacity:

| Keypad runs on first visit | canvas content changes 3.3s → 5.4s, holds to 6.0s |

+const browser = await chromium.launch();

+const page = await ctx.newPage();
+await page.goto(URL, { waitUntil: "load" });

+const waitFor = async (sel, min, timeout) => {
+  const t0 = Date.now();
+  while (Date.now() - t0 < timeout) {
+    if ((await page.evaluate(opacity(sel))) >= min) return true;
+    await page.waitForTimeout(100);

+await page.waitForTimeout(1_100);
+await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/02-wheel-mid.png` });
+await page.waitForTimeout(2_200);
+await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/03-wheel-open.png` });
+
+/* wait for the intro to finish: the wheel fades back out */
+const t0 = Date.now();
+while (Date.now() - t0 < 20_000) {

+  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
+}

+await page.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/04-rest.png` });
+
+console.log(`keypad lit: ${lit}, wheel turned: ${turning}`);
+
+await browser.close();

Fixed — the keypad you saw on `/signup` was the hero's **Sign in hover reaction**, left switched on by a hover that was too quick for it.

## What was happening

`signInHover` lights the nine flat keys with a per-key GSAP delay (`(col + row) × 0.0618s`). On mouseleave it asks them all to go dark with `overwrite: "auto"` — but auto-overwrite only stops tweens that have **already started**. A pointer that crosses "Sign in" for a few dozen milliseconds (or moves from Sign in to Sign up) leaves the not-yet-started delayed tweens queued; they fire *after* the off-tween finished, so their keys light up and stay lit. That's the staircase — six keys in your screenshot, three in my shorter flicks:

```
dwell 40ms   → keys[0 0 0 0 0 1 0 1 1] on /signup   (before the fix)
dwell 100ms  → keys[0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 1] on /signup
```

The vault is mounted once in `VaultLayout`, so those lit keys rode it onto the form page. The same flick also left the dashed teal Sign-in connector half-drawn across the gap to the keypad (that faint line in your screenshot) and could leave the flat keypad `visibility: hidden`.

## The fix

[HeroVault.tsx](src/components/HeroVault.tsx) — each key's previous tween is killed before a new one starts, so a queued delayed tween can no longer fire behind an off. Added `resetCtas()`, which drops the key/glow/LED/hinge/seam/connector tweens, puts every hotspot back to rest, removes the connector path and restores the keypad's visibility.

[HeroButtons.tsx](src/components/HeroButtons.tsx) — calls `resetCtas()` as the hero unmounts, so nothing the hero lit can follow the persistent vault to another route.

## Verified

```
flick 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 140ms   keys all 0 on hero AND on /signup
full hover (900ms)                all nine lit; leaving signin clears them
after Sign up                     keys 0, glow 0, clip 0, connector path removed, keypad visible
reduced motion, direct /signup    clean
/ → /signin → back                keys 0, keypad visible, clip off
role → Change role → Back         1440 + 390: h1/CTA/body/chips opacity 1, 0 ghosts, vault-x 61.8
```

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean. The keypad on `/signup` now sits dark, with only the little green LED that's part of the vault art.

Five files are modified and uncommitted: the two above plus the earlier [Hero.tsx](src/components/Hero.tsx), [VaultLayout.tsx](src/layouts/VaultLayout.tsx) and [Signup.tsx](src/pages/Signup.tsx) from the back-navigation fix. I removed my temporary probe scripts and screenshots.

The other hover in that family — the wheel clip on Sign up — has the same "one clip owns the vault" wiring, so it's worth a quick sweep for similar leftovers on the way back from `/signin`.

- **CSS** — plain, hand-written, no Tailwind directives even though the plugin is installed: tokens, hero, signup, [signin.css](src/styles/signin.css)
- **JSON** for config/data: [keypad-manifest.json](src/config/keypad-manifest.json), package.json
- **HTML** once, in [index.html](index.html)

Around the app, three more:

- **JavaScript (ESM, `.mjs`)** — 37 throwaway verification scripts in `scripts/`, run with plain `node` + Playwright (screenshots, frame comparison, CLS/overflow checks). Not shipped.
- **JavaScript/TypeScript in the e2e specs** — 4 files in `tests/`, both `.spec.ts`.
- **Bash** for the git/checkpoint commands; **SVG** markup inside the JSX for the wheel seams and connectors.

Data formats touched incidentally: PNG screenshots, WebP/PNG frame sequences for both clips, WOFF2 fonts.

No backend language yet — mock auth is a TS function, and there's no server code in the repo.

Nothing is on GitHub yet — `git remote -v` is empty, so this has never been pushed anywhere. Here's exactly how I'd do it, in the order that avoids the usual traps.

## What the repo looks like right now

- 7 local branches, 6 tags, **573 tracked files**, `.git` is 25 MB.
- **`main` is a direct ancestor of `feat/signin`**, 37 commits behind. A fast-forward merge puts all the work on `main` with no merge commit.
- You're on `feat/signin` with **7 uncommitted files**: the VaultLance rename (4 docs + `Signin.tsx` + `Signup.tsx`) and one `.gitignore` line (`/freebuff-sites-build/`).
- No `.env`, no secrets in the tree. `.gitignore` already keeps out `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `test-results/`, `docs/hero-shots/` (224 MB of screenshots), `backup/`, `freebuff-sites-build/`, `dev.log`.
- The app's real assets are tracked: `public/` is 9.4 MB across 447 files, including all 96 `public/Keypad frames/*.webp` and `public/vault-frames/`. A fresh clone runs.
- Identity is set to `Ahmed-A-Anwar <ahmedidea12@gmail.com>`. No `gh` CLI, no credential helper configured.

## Decision you make first: what goes on `main`

Two sane shapes, pick one before pushing:

- **Fast-forward (what I'd do).** `main` becomes the current `feat/signin` tip, feature branches stay local or get pushed as history. GitHub's default branch shows the finished app.
- **Push everything.** `git push --all` puts all 7 branches up. Honest history, but `main` still shows the old hero and the repo looks abandoned at first glance.

## The steps

**1. Commit the pending rename first.** It exists on no commit yet, so no branch push will carry it:

```bash
git add design-plan.md docs/PLAN.md docs/RESEARCH.md docs/hero.md src/pages/Signin.tsx src/pages/Signup.tsx
git commit -m "docs: rename the product to VaultLance AI"
git add .gitignore && git commit -m "chore: ignore the sites build output"
```

**2. Create the repository empty.** On github.com → New repository → name it, **Private or Public**, and add **no** README, `.gitignore` or license. Those three create a commit that makes your first push a non-fast-forward mess.

**3. Add the remote and authenticate.**

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/Ahmed-A-Anwar/<repo>.git
git remote -v
```

For auth on Windows, either let Git Credential Manager pop up a browser on the first push (it ships with Git for Windows — you have no helper configured, so it'll be offered then), or install the CLI and use `gh auth login` once, which also writes the credential helper for you. Don't paste a personal access token into a file in the repo.

**4. First push — `main` only.**

```bash
git checkout main
git merge --ff-only feat/signin      # verified possible: main is an ancestor
git push -u origin main
```

`-u` matters: it sets upstream so later `git push` / `git pull` need no arguments.

**5. Then the rest, if you want them visible.**

```bash
git push origin feat/signin feat/signup-polish feat/signup-transition feat/keypad-clip feat/mobile-layout feat/wheel-clip
git push --tags        # hero-v1-stable … signin-v1-pre, all 6
```

Tags are worth pushing — `signin-v1-pre` is a rollback point you've already used.

**6. Settings.** Confirm `main` is the default branch (Settings → General). If anyone else touches it, protect `main` and require a PR; for a solo demo repo, skip that.

**7. Verify what actually landed**, not just that the push exited 0:

```bash
git ls-remote --heads origin          # branches and their SHAs
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | wc -l     # ≈573 tracked files
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -c "Keypad frames"   # 96, the clip ships
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -E "^(dist|node_modules)/" || echo "no build output, correct"
```

Then clone it somewhere fresh and run `npm ci && npm run dev` — that's the only real proof the published repo is the working app, not just a plausible file list.

## Traps specific to this repo

- `backup/` is gitignored, so the VaultLance edits I made inside `backup/hero-v1` and `hero-v2` stay local and will **not** appear on GitHub. If those archives matter, they need `git add -f` or the ignore rule relaxed.
- `docs/hero-shots/` (224 MB — every signin/signup screenshot and frame sequence) is ignored on purpose. Nothing in `src/` reads from it, so the app is unaffected; just know that the screenshots in my earlier reports won't be on GitHub.
- `dist/` and `freebuff-sites-build/` are ignored, so no build output leaks into the repo. Anyone cloning has to `npm ci` first.
- No LFS needed: the largest tracked file is 547 KB (`public/vault-frames/f_001_probe.png`), well under GitHub's 100 MB per-file and 1 GB soft repo limits.
- `public/Keypad frames/` has a space in the folder name. Git is fine with it, the manifest URLs already percent-encode to `%20`, but you can't paste those paths into a shell without quoting.
- Line endings: git warns `LF will be replaced by CRLF` because `core.autocrlf` is on. It works, but adding a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` before the first push saves a churny diff later. That's a real change to the repo, so I'd ask before adding it.

Rollback if a push is wrong: `git push origin --delete <branch>` for a branch, and force-push only the branch you just created (`git push --force-with-lease origin main`), never a shared one.

Progress note:
The H1 now renders in Fraunces's display cut, but the opsz change rewrapped the headline from four lines to three. That is a layout change the brief's "no other change" rules out, so flag it: it is the one consequence of the requested values.

## The change

[hero.css:214](src/styles/hero.css#L214), `.hero-h1` only:

```css
letter-spacing: -0.01em;                                  /* was -0.02em */
font-variant-ligatures: none;                             /* + */
font-feature-settings: "liga" 0, "clig" 0, "dlig" 0;      /* + */
font-variation-settings: "opsz" 96, "WONK" 0;             /* + */
```

Computed after: `font-variant-ligatures: none`, `font-feature-settings: "clig" 0, "dlig" 0, "liga" 0`, `font-variation-settings: "WONK" 0, "opsz" 96`, `letter-spacing: -0.6768px`.

One thing worth knowing: the H1 was inheriting `h1 { font-variation-settings: "wdth" 118 }` from [app.css:18](src/styles/app.css#L18). I measured whether that axis does anything for this face — `wdth` 100 vs 118 gives **identical** width (1336.95px both), because Fraunces carries opsz/wght/SOFT/WONK and no `wdth`. So overriding it is inert. The axes that *do* exist, measured at 96px on the same string: opsz 9 → 1643.53px, opsz 96 → 1336.95px, opsz 144 → 1315.69px; WONK 0 → 1336.91 vs 1 → 1336.95; SOFT 0 → 1336.95 vs 100 → 1382.88. All four requested declarations are real, not no-ops.

The full-axis file is why opsz and WONK bite at all.

573 tracked files. `public/` is 447 of them and ~17 MB; `docs/` is 2.7 MB; everything else is about 200 KB of source, scripts and config.

Fixed — Codebuff is gone from the contributors list. Here's why it was there and what I did.

## Why it appeared

GitHub's Insights → Contributors list isn't built from commit authors alone. It also credits `Co-Authored-By:` trailers, which is the standard way to give a co-author commit credit — and once that email is tied to a GitHub account, that account shows up in the list and in the contribution graph.

Six of your 39 commits ended with:

```
🤖 Generated with Codebuff
Co-Authored-By: Codebuff <noreply@codebuff.com>
```

So GitHub read each of them as "Ahmed wrote this with a co-author named Codebuff" and listed Codebuff alongside you. The commits themselves were 100% yours; only the trailer was extra.

## What I changed

I rewrote the commit messages across the whole history to drop those two lines, then force-pushed `main`:

```
6ca1946 → c1abfa5   main (forced update)
```

Verification, before pushing:

- **Content untouched.** All 39 old trees hash-identical to their 39 new counterparts; `git diff pre-attribution-rewrite main` is empty.
- **Only attribution removed.** Every message compared byte-for-byte against the original with just the Codebuff lines stripped — 0 message mismatches, 0 tree mismatches.
- **Remote clean.** `git log origin/main --grep=Codebuff` → 0. Commit count still 39.

Then, through the GitHub API after the push:

```
Ahmed-A-Anwar (39)
```

That's the live contributors endpoint, not a local reading — Codebuff is absent and you hold all 39 commits.

## Things to know

- **Every commit hash changed.** Local `main` and `origin/main` are both `c1abfa5` and in sync. If you have another clone or a fork, it won't fast-forward — re-clone it rather than pulling.
- **Your tags moved too** (`hero-v1-stable`, `signin-v1-pre`, `signup-v1-stable`, etc.) since they point at rewritten commits. None of them were on the remote, so nothing to reconcile there.
- **One local rescue tag exists:** `pre-attribution-rewrite` → `6ca1946`, the old history. It is *not* pushed. Rollback is `git reset --hard pre-attribution-rewrite`. When you're happy, `git tag -d pre-attribution-rewrite` removes it — and **don't run a blanket `git push --tags`** while it exists, or the old commits travel up with it (that wouldn't restore the contributor entry, since the graph follows the default branch, but it defeats the cleanup).
- **Going forward I won't add that footer.** The "Generated with Codebuff / Co-Authored-By" block is a default, not a requirement — you've now asked for it gone, so new commits here will end with the message itself. If you ever want it back deliberately, say so.
- Your `.gitignore` line (`/freebuff-sites-build/`) is still uncommitted and I left it exactly as it was.

# VaultLance AI hero — design plan

## Subject
VaultLance AI landing hero: vault photography + goldenratio layout + entrance timeline.

## Color
- ink #0E1520
- slate #4B5663
- steel #8A95A1
- brass #B8893A
- brass-light #E2B867
- teal #12A5B5
- success #1F9D6B
- bg gradient sampled from frame (top -> bottom).

## Type
- Display/headline: Fraunces 600, optical auto, -0.02em, 1.05, clamp(42, 4.7vw, 68).
- Mono labels: JetBrains Mono 12px uppercase 0.14em.
- Body: Inter 400 16/1.618 max 44ch.
- Buttons: Inter 600 16px 0.01em.

## Layout
- Desktop: 38.2% text | 61.8% vault. Vault focal wheel center at 61.8% x, 50% y.
- Buttons row on 61.8% horizontal golden line from top.
- Tablet/mobile: vault first 100%, text below, buttons stacked full width.
- Text column left padding 89px on desktop; 21px on tablet/mobile.
- Vault overflow visible; soft shadow is part of the image — no extra shadow.

## Motion
- GSAP entrance timeline, durations from {0.236,0.382,0.618,1,1.618,2.618}.
- Idle loops: vault float 6.18s, teal glow 2.618s, shimmer 1.618s/6.18s, parallax lerp 0.08.
- Reduced motion: final state only.
- Button hover/tap reactions with vault hotspots; mobile uses tap not hover.

## Build steps
1. Sample frame colors and confirm hotspot positions.
2. Add fonts (Fraunces, JetBrains Mono, Inter) to index.html.
3. Build Hero.tsx + Hero.css.
4. Update Landing to render Hero above VaultSequence.
5. Wire GSAP entrance + idle loops.
6. Wire Sign up / Sign in reactions.
7. Verify.

There's now an entry gate: the page loads behind a curtain, shows real progress, and only then hands over — so the hero entrance and the self-demoing vault start when every frame they draw is already decoded, instead of streaming in front of the visitor.

## How it behaves

1. **A static curtain is up before the bundle arrives.** [index.html](index.html) holds a pre-React overlay (wordmark + an indeterminate brass hairline) that only appears on `/`, when motion isn't reduced, and when this tab hasn't already been let in. Without it, the finished hero paints first and *then* the loader covers it — that flash is exactly the bug I hit on my first pass, so the curtain now lives in the HTML.
2. **React's gate takes over with real numbers.** [Boot.tsx](src/components/Boot.tsx) removes the static copy, then polls the actual clip players and reports percent: `LOADING THE MECHANISM · N`, switching to `READY` at 100.
3. **Progress is measured on the players themselves**, not on a guessed total — `bankedTo()` on the wheel clip (all 81 frames) and on the keypad clip up to K1 (48 of 96, which is as far as the intro or a Sign-in click ever draws). No duplicate decode pass, so the gate costs nothing extra.
4. **Release order matters:** the gate opens (the hero entrance starts *under* a still-opaque curtain), then two frames later the curtain fades over 0.618s. Reversed, you'd see the finished hero for a frame before the entrance reset it.
5. **The vault demo waits for the gate too**, so nothing animates behind the curtain — its 2.618s beat is measured from release rather than from mount.

## What it deliberately skips

- Reduced motion — no curtain, no gate, no clips (there is nothing to bank).
- Any route other than `/`, so `/signup`, `/signin`, `/vault/*` load as before.
- Every later load in the same tab session (`sessionStorage: vl-booted`), so a reload or a return from `/signup` doesn't replay it.
- Phones: the keypad clip is desktop-only, so the gate waits for the wheel only.
- A 25s ceiling, so one lost frame can't strand the page; it logs `[boot] entering — timed out waiting for the clips` and lets you in.

## Verified

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both clean; the built `dist/index.html` carries the static curtain.
- Playwright run with every `.webp` delayed 90ms: curtain present at 175 ms (before the bundle), React gate at 1.1 s, progress `10 → … → 99 → 100`, gate gone at 6.7 s, hero opacity climbing `0.35 → 1` *while* the curtain was still up, then `[boot] entering — frames banked` and `[fx] vault intro: keypad, then one wheel turn` in that order. Reload in the same tab: no gate.
- Same checks for reduced motion (no gate at all), 390px (gate waits on the wheel only), and a direct `/signup` load (no gate).
- `npm run test:e2e`: **8 passed, 8 failed**. All 8 failures are pre-existing stale specs for the retired scroll landing — they look for the "Put it to Test" payoff CTA and caption scenes, and [Landing.tsx](src/pages/Landing.tsx) renders only `Hero`; `VaultSequence` isn't mounted anywhere. I left them alone rather than rewrite tests outside this change. The 320px no-overflow test on `/` passes, so the overlay adds no horizontal scroll.

## Files

New: [Boot.tsx](src/components/Boot.tsx). Changed: [vaultScene.tsx](src/lib/vaultScene.tsx) (adds `booted` + a clips handle), [VaultLayout.tsx](src/layouts/VaultLayout.tsx) (owns the gate stages), [Hero.tsx](src/components/Hero.tsx) (entrance gated on `booted`), [HeroButtons.tsx](src/components/HeroButtons.tsx) (publishes the clip measurements, intro waits for release), [hero.css](src/styles/hero.css) (gate styles), [index.html](index.html).

Nothing is committed, and none of it is deployed — push to `main` and Vercel will rebuild. Two tunables if the curtain feels long or short: `MIN_MS` (900) and `MAX_MS` (25000) at the top of [Boot.tsx](src/components/Boot.tsx). The cost of this approach is honest: ~7.9 MB of frames is now fetched before you're let in, where before it trickled in during the entrance.

One bit of housekeeping: replacing the preview stopped the old dev server, so I started a fresh one (`npm run dev`, now registered in the Preview tab) — it's running and serving the gate.

import { chromium } from "@playwright/test";

const URL = process.env.LIVE_URL ?? "https://vault-lance-ai.vercel.app/";

    if (/\[boot\]|\[fx\]/.test(text)) seen.push(`${String(Date.now() - t0).padStart(6)}ms ${text}`);
  });

  await page.goto(URL, { waitUntil: "commit" });

  const marks = {};
  const watch = async (key, fn, timeout = 60000) => {
    try {
      await page.waitForFunction(fn, null, { timeout, polling: 100 });
      marks[key] = Date.now() - t0;
    } catch {
      marks[key] = "timeout";
    }
  };
  await watch("gateVisible", () => !!document.querySelector(".boot-hub-num"), 30000);
  await watch("count10", () => {
    const t = document.querySelector(".boot-count-num")?.textContent ?? "";
    return parseInt(t, 10) >= 10;
  });
  await watch("countHalf", () => {
    const t = document.querySelector(".boot-count-num")?.textContent ?? "";
    const [b, total] = t.split("/").map((s) => parseInt(s, 10));
    return total > 0 && b >= total / 2;
  });
  await watch("gateGone", () => !document.querySelector('[data-testid="boot"]'), 60000);
  await watch("headlineIn", () => {
    const el = document.querySelector(".hero-h1 .word-inner");
    return el ? Number(getComputedStyle(el).opacity) > 0.9 : false;
  }, 30000);

  const state = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    stored: sessionStorage.getItem("vl-booted"),
    hero: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(".hero-page")).opacity,
  }));
  console.log(`== ${vp.width}x${vp.height} ==`, marks, state);
  console.log("   " + seen.join("\n   "));
  await ctx.close();
}

await browser.close();
"}}

/* canvasFeather.ts — the phone band crops the vault frame top and bottom, and a
   CSS mask is not a dependable way to soften that crop: engines that have not
   shipped mask-image drop it and leave the frame's own shadow cut off dead
   straight, and WebKit has been known to paint the masked-out rows black instead
   of transparent. Writing the fade into the canvas pixels instead works the same
   everywhere, so that is what the phone layout does. */

/* same breakpoint as the phone rules in hero.css */
export const phoneBand = () =>
  typeof window !== "undefined" && window.innerWidth <= 767;

/* erase a soft 21px band at the top and bottom, in the canvas's own coordinate
   space (call it while the drawing transform is still the CSS-pixel one) */
export const featherBand = (
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  w: number,
  h: number,
  px = 21,
) => {
  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
  const edge = Math.min(0.5, px / h);
  const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, h);
  g.addColorStop(0, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)");
  g.addColorStop(edge, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)");
  g.addColorStop(1 - edge, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)");
  g.addColorStop(1, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)");
  ctx.save();
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "destination-out";
  ctx.fillStyle = g;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
  ctx.restore();
};

   CSS mask is not a dependable way to soften that crop: engines that have not
   shipped mask-image drop it and leave the frame's own shadow cut off dead
   straight, WebKit has been known to paint the masked-out rows black, and a mask
   on an element that is being translated can leave a one-pixel seam where the
   layer ends. Writing the fade into the canvas pixels instead works the same
   everywhere, so that is what the phone layout does (the mask is switched off
   there in hero.css). */

/* same breakpoint as the phone rules in hero.css */
export const phoneBand = () =>
  typeof window !== "undefined" && window.innerWidth <= 767;

/* erase a soft band at the top and bottom, in the canvas's own coordinate
   space (call it while the drawing transform is still the CSS-pixel one).
   28-56px, or 12% of a short band: the frame's contact shadow sits well inside
   that, so a crop through it fades out instead of ending in a line. */
export const featherBand = (
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  w: number,
  h: number,
  px = 0,
) => {
  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
  const band = px > 0 ? px : Math.round(Math.min(56, Math.max(28, h * 0.12)));
  const edge = Math.min(0.5, band / h);
  const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, h);
  g.addColorStop(0, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)");
  g.addColorStop(edge, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)");
  g.addColorStop(1 - edge, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)");
  g.addColorStop(1, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)");
  ctx.save();
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "destination-out";
  ctx.fillStyle = g;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
  ctx.restore();
};

/* the phone band's feather, read live: one canvas serves every width, so this
   decides per paint rather than once when a player is created */
export const featherPhoneBand = (
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  w: number,
  h: number,
) => {
  if (phoneBand()) featherBand(ctx, w, h);
};

**Why your phone still showed the old behaviour:** the two earlier commits only reached GitHub at 01:41 and 01:51, and your screenshot/message came at ~01:45 — so the phone was almost certainly still running the build from before the fix. **What I changed now**, so it doesn't depend on that timing or on one browser's media-query quirks:

- [HeroButtons.tsx](src/components/HeroButtons.tsx) no longer decides tap-vs-hover from `matchMedia`. Each press records the pointer that opened it (`pointerType`), and a touch commits immediately; hover previews only run for a mouse, keyboard focus still previews where hovering exists. This also covers iPads with a trackpad, in-app browsers and foldables that claim `hover: hover` while a finger is tapping. The touchstart "arming" fetches are gone too.

  if (hour < 12) return "morning";
  if (hour < 18) return "afternoon";
  return "evening";
}

export function decisionLine(audited: number): string {
  if (audited === 0) return "ALL CLEAR";
  return `${audited} VAULT${audited === 1 ? "" : "S"} NEED${audited === 1 ? "S" : ""} YOUR DECISION`;
}

export function Greeting({ firstName, audited }: { firstName: string; audited: number | null }) {
  const part = partOfDay();

    <div className="dash-greeting" data-enter="greeting">

          <span className="dash-skel dash-greeting-skel" aria-hidden="true" />
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className="dash-eyebrow-mark" aria-hidden="true" />
            {decisionLine(audited)}
          </>
        )}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

  await ctx.addInitScript((s) => {
    try {
      window.sessionStorage.setItem("vl.dash.session", s);
    } catch {}
  }, session);
  const page = await ctx.newPage();
  await page.goto(`${URL}${path}${extra}`, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
  return { ctx, page };
}

async function measure(page) {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const r = (sel) => {
      const el = document.querySelector(sel);
      if (!el) return null;
      const b = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { x: +b.x.toFixed(1), y: +b.y.toFixed(1), w: +b.width.toFixed(1), h: +b.height.toFixed(1), bottom: +b.bottom.toFixed(1) };

      return { text: el.textContent, h: +b.height.toFixed(1), y: +b.y.toFixed(1) };

      rail: r(".dash-rail"),
      strip: r(".dash-strip"),
      emptyFig: r(".dash-empty-fig"),
      emptyImg: r(".dash-empty-img"),
    };
  });
}

const results = {};

  ["1280", 1280, 720],
  ["390", 390, 844],
]) {

}

- "/vault/:id" renders the room. Not signed in goes to "/signin".
  Freelancer role goes to /dashboard. Unknown id shows a not-found state
  with a Back button.
- Old "/playground?vault=<id>" redirects to "/vault/<id>". "/playground"
  alone stays a placeholder.

STATE MACHINE (from vault.status in the mock API)
awaiting_payment: chat LOCKED (overlay with padlock and the text
 "Authorize payment to start the audit."), checks QUEUED, decision panel
 shows Authorize payment.
held: chat OPEN, checks idle with a "Run all checks" button, Approve
 disabled with the hint "Run the audit first." Reject enabled.
audited: chat OPEN, checks show results, Approve and Reject enabled.
unlocked: files unlocked with Download buttons, chat read-only, decision
 panel shows the receipt.
voided: everything dimmed to 60%, VOIDED ribbon, chat read-only, no actions.
Stepper phases: Uploaded, Authorized, Audited, Captured, Unlocked.
awaiting_payment = Uploaded done. held = Authorized done. audited = Audited
done. unlocked = all done. Captured and Unlocked light 0.618s apart.

Vaultpay: backend handoff

Scope: the client dashboard data layer and the vault audit room. Every backend behavior described here is simulated in the browser today. Nothing below is wired to a real service.

1. What exists today

The UI reads and writes through the functions in src/lib/api.ts. Each function names the endpoint it will call once the mock is replaced. The data lives in module-level arrays and resets on reload. Three other modules hold local state: src/lib/store.tsx (the ledger store and timers), src/lib/mockAuth.ts (sign-in and session) and src/lib/seed.ts (demo copy and fixtures).

The backend has to be built from scratch. The contracts in section 3 are the ones the UI already assumes, so the frontend can switch from the mock to real calls without changing its components.

3. Data contracts

These types are declared in src/lib/api.ts and src/lib/store.tsx. The JSON a route returns should match them exactly.

Vault

{
  id: string,              // e.g. "v_logo_pack"
  project: string,
  freelancer: string,
  amountUSD: number,       // whole dollars in the mock
  status: "awaiting_payment" | "held" | "audited" | "unlocked" | "voided",
  createdAt: number,       // epoch ms
  paypalOrderId?: string   // set once funds are authorized
}

LedgerEvent

{
  id: string,
  ts: number,              // epoch ms
  type: "PAYMENT.AUTHORIZED" | "PAYMENT.CAPTURED" | "PAYMENT.VOIDED"
      | "FILES.UNLOCKED" | "AUDIT.COMPLETED",
  vaultId: string,
  label: string,
  amountUSD?: number,
  paypalId?: string
}

Kpis

{ fundsHeld: number, awaitingReview: number, unlocked: number }

fundsHeld sums amountUSD over vaults in held or audited. awaitingReview counts audited. unlocked counts unlocked.

Room detail (GET /v1/vaults/{id})

{
  vault: Vault,
  files: VaultFile[],          // { id, name, kind: "url" | "folder" | "file", meta, url?, children? }
  checks: VaultCheck[],        // { id, name, detail, source, result, state, rows: { label, value }[] }
  messages: ChatMessage[],
  suggestions: string[],       // starter questions for the room
  questionsUsed: number,
  questionLimit: number        // 15 in the mock (QUESTION_LIMIT, api.ts:400)
}

Errors

The mock throws ApiError (api.ts:47) with one of four kinds: network, conflict, not_found, state. A state error means the action is not allowed for the vault's current status. expectStatus (api.ts:199) produces these, with messages such as "This vault cannot be approved while it is held." The real backend should return the same four kinds so the UI shows the same messages.

4. State rules

The status transitions below are the ones the mock enforces. Each write is refused unless the vault is in the listed status.

ActionAllowed fromResult statusLedger event
authorizeawaiting_paymentheldPAYMENT.AUTHORIZED
audit / checks:runheldauditedAUDIT.COMPLETED
capture (approve)auditedunlockedPAYMENT.CAPTURED, then FILES.UNLOCKED
void (reject)audited, heldvoidedPAYMENT.VOIDED

A vault that is already audited or unlocked opens its room with the check results already settled (api.ts:573). Any other status shows the checks as queued.

5. Mock behaviour to replace

  • Latency: every read and write waits 300 to 618 ms (latency(), api.ts:175). ?slow=1 stretches it to 2600 ms so the skeletons show.
  • Failure rate: 5% of calls throw a network error (FAIL_RATE, api.ts:173). The real API does not need this; the UI's error states should be tested against real failures.
  • Seed data: four vaults (api.ts:80). ?empty=1 starts with no vaults. The booking-app room has fixed files, checks and suggestions (api.ts:406); other rooms use a generic seed (api.ts:543).
  • Paypal ids: paypalId() makes ids in the form 8XK12345AB678901C (api.ts:~45). The real ids come from PayPal.
  • Audit checks: runChecks (api.ts:593) runs the checks one at a time with timings of 618, 1000, 1618 and 1000 ms, then marks the vault audited. The real runner will report progress by SSE or polling.
  • Agent answers: askAI (api.ts:623) matches keywords in answerFor (api.ts:642) and streams the reply to onToken. Each room has a question limit of 15.
  • Join code: joinVault accepts only DEMO-1234 and refuses a second join with a conflict error (api.ts:290 onwards).
  • Ledger timers: the store schedules its own replay timers (store.tsx:95 and store.tsx:118). These belong in the client and can stay once events arrive over SSE.
  • Sign-in: signIn (mockAuth.ts:83) accepts any email and password that pass validation. Emails starting with fail@ are refused. Passwords need at least 8 characters (MIN_PASSWORD, mockAuth.ts:65). Sessions are kept in browser storage through readSession, writeSession and clearSession (mockAuth.ts:31 to 62).

6. Open decisions

  1. Where the API runs: the frontend is a Vite and React single-page app with react-router-dom, so API routes need a separate host. Choose between Next.js route handlers and a standalone Node or Edge API. The JSON contracts in section 3 are the same either way.
  2. Payment provider: the event labels and paypalOrderId assume PayPal. Confirm the provider before building the authorize, capture and void routes.
  3. Audit runner: the mock runs checks in the browser. The real runner needs an owner, a queue and a way to report progress.

    Vaultpay: backend handoff

    +

    Scope: the client dashboard data layer and the vault audit room. Every backend behavior described here is simulated in the browser today. Nothing below is wired to a real service.

    + +

    1. What exists today

    +

    The UI reads and writes through the functions in src/lib/api.ts. Each function names the endpoint it will call once the mock is replaced. The data lives in module-level arrays and resets on reload. Three other modules hold local state: src/lib/store.tsx (the ledger store and timers), src/lib/mockAuth.ts (sign-in and session) and src/lib/seed.ts (demo copy and fixtures).

    +

    + +

    2. Endpoints

    +

    3. Data contracts

    +

    These types are declared in src/lib/api.ts and src/lib/store.tsx. The JSON a route returns should match them exactly.

    + +

    Vault

    +
    {
+  id: string,              // e.g. "v_logo_pack"
+  project: string,
+  freelancer: string,
+  amountUSD: number,       // whole dollars in the mock
+  status: "awaiting_payment" | "held" | "audited" | "unlocked" | "voided",
+  createdAt: number,       // epoch ms
+  paypalOrderId?: string   // set once funds are authorized
+}
    + +

    LedgerEvent

    +
    {
+  id: string,
+  ts: number,              // epoch ms
+  type: "PAYMENT.AUTHORIZED" | "PAYMENT.CAPTURED" | "PAYMENT.VOIDED"
+      | "FILES.UNLOCKED" | "AUDIT.COMPLETED",
+  vaultId: string,
+  label: string,
+  amountUSD?: number,
+  paypalId?: string
+}
    + +

    Kpis

    +
    { fundsHeld: number, awaitingReview: number, unlocked: number }
    +

    fundsHeld sums amountUSD over vaults in held or audited. awaitingReview counts audited. unlocked counts unlocked.

    + +

    Room detail (GET /v1/vaults/{id})

    +
    {
+  vault: Vault,
+  files: VaultFile[],          // { id, name, kind: "url" | "folder" | "file", meta, url?, children? }
+  checks: VaultCheck[],        // { id, name, detail, source, result, state, rows: { label, value }[] }
+  messages: ChatMessage[],
+  suggestions: string[],       // starter questions for the room
+  questionsUsed: number,
+  questionLimit: number        // 15 in the mock (QUESTION_LIMIT, api.ts:400)
+}
    + +

    Errors

    +

    The mock throws ApiError (api.ts:47) with one of four kinds: network, conflict, not_found, state. A state error means the action is not allowed for the vault's current status. expectStatus (api.ts:199) produces these, with messages such as "This vault cannot be approved while it is held." The real backend should return the same four kinds so the UI shows the same messages.

    + +

    4. State rules

    +

    The status transitions below are the ones the mock enforces. Each write is refused unless the vault is in the listed status.

/reset-password. Reuse the persistent vault layout. Real email sending and
real token handling come later from the backend.

SCOPE LOCK (highest priority)
- Do NOT change the hero, the wheel or keypad clips, /signup, the
  dashboard, the audit room, colors, fonts, tokens, copy outside this
  page, or my frames.
- Allowed edits outside new files: the "Forgot password?" link in the
  /signin page (href only), src/lib/mockAuth.ts (additive), App.tsx
  (routes only), src/config/fx.ts (additive flag).
- New files go under src/pages/auth/ and src/components/auth/. Reuse the
  existing auth card, input, primary button, toast, wordmark and Back link
  components. Do not duplicate them.
- No new dependencies. No backend calls.
- If something needs a deviation, STOP and report it. Wait for my answer.

STEP 0: SNAPSHOT
git add -A && git commit -m "checkpoint: before forgot password"
git tag forgot-v0-pre
git checkout -b feat/forgot-password
Report the hash. Rollback: git reset --hard forgot-v0-pre.
Commit after each slice.
Flag: FX.forgotFlow = true in fx.ts. false restores the old link
behavior (href "#", disabled look is NOT needed, just the old state).

GOLDEN SYSTEM (identical to /signin)
phi 1.618, 1/phi 0.618, 1/phi^2 0.382.
- Vault anchor "--vault-x": all three routes = 76.4%. The vault stays
  mounted when moving between /signin, /forgot-password and
  /reset-password (verify with a mount log that fires once).
- Card: 453px wide, centered horizontally on the 38.2% line and
  vertically on the 50% line. Padding 34, radius 13, glass:
  rgba(255,255,255,0.35), blur 12px, 1px #8A95A1,
  shadow 0 8px 21px rgba(14,21,32,0.08).
- Inputs and buttons: height 55, gap 13, radius 13.
- Type: H1 42px Fraunces 600, line-height 1.05, letter-spacing -0.01em,
  ligatures off. Body 16px / 1.618 Inter. Mono 12px JetBrains Mono,
  uppercase, tracking 0.14em.
- Spacing: 8 / 13 / 21 / 34 / 55 / 89. Durations only from
  0.236 / 0.382 / 0.618 / 1 / 1.618 / 2.618 s. Resend cooldown 55s.
- Wordmark "VaultLance AI" top left and the "Back" link under it, same as
  /signin. On /forgot-password, Back goes to /signin.

COLORS (existing tokens)
ink #0E1520, slate #4B5663, steel #8A95A1, brass #B8893A / #E2B867,
teal #12A5B5, success #1F9D6B, danger #C4453D. Page gradient #C9D0D2 to
#E1E7E8. Use #0A6A74 for small teal text and #7A551A for small brass
text, as in the audit room. Check contrast on every text and fill pair.
Report ratios. If any is under 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), STOP.

SLICE 1: /forgot-password (request screen)
Content:
- H1 "Forgot your code?"
- Sub "Enter your email. We'll send a link to reset your password."
- Email input (label visible, autocomplete="email", inputmode="email").
- Primary button "Send reset link" (brass gradient, 55px).
- Ghost link under it: arrow-left icon plus "Back to sign in".
- Mono microcopy: SANDBOX DEMO · NO REAL EMAIL IS SENT.
Left strip (0 to 23.6% of viewport, left padding 55, centered on 50%,
hidden under 1100px): one mono status line, same style as /signin.
Text: "KEYPAD LOCKED" with a 13px steel dot. States change it below.
Validation: email format on blur and on submit. Inline error under the
field. Focus the first invalid field. Empty field shows "Enter your
email."
Behavior:
- Submit: spinner in the button for 0.618s min, then the "sent" state.
- Security rule: the result is the same whether or not the email exists.
  Never reveal if an account exists.
- Network error (5% mock chance, flag-controlled by FX.mockErrors if it
  exists): inline error "Couldn't send. Try again." with the button
  re-enabled.
- After 3 sends in one session, show "Too many attempts. Try again in
  55 seconds." and disable the button with a countdown.
Button effects (reuse the brass primary exactly): lift -2px, shimmer sweep
once 1.618s, arrow nudges +3px, shadow grows, 0.382s. Press scale 0.97,
0.236s. Focus ring teal 3px at 3px offset.
Entrance from /signin: old card out (x -34, opacity 0, 0.382s), new card in
(x 34 to 0, opacity, 0.382s). Form children rise y 21 to 0, stagger 0.1s
starting 0.236s after the card. The vault does not move.
Direct load: skip the intro, show the final state.
- Commit.

SLICE 2: "LINK SENT" STATE (same route, same card)
Cross-fade the card content 0.382s with x -21 to 0. Content:
- A 55px circle icon (envelope with a check) in teal on teal 12%, the
  check draws in with stroke-dashoffset 0.618s.
- H1 "Check your inbox."
- Body "If an account exists for <email>, a reset link is on its way. It
  expires in 30 minutes." Show the email in mono, ink, ellipsis if long.
- Primary button "Back to sign in" (brass, 55px).
- Secondary glass button "Resend link", disabled for 55 seconds with a
  mono countdown inside "RESEND IN 55". A 2px teal progress line under
  the button drains over 55s. When ready, the button enables with a
  0.382s teal ring pulse. Resend shows a toast "Link sent again." and
  restarts the cooldown.
- Ghost link "Use a different email" returns to the form with the email
  prefilled and focused.
- Mono microcopy: CHECK SPAM · LINK EXPIRES IN 30 MINUTES
- Focus moves to the H1 (tabindex -1) when this state appears. The change
  is announced via an aria-live polite region.
Vault reaction: the keypad hotspot flashes teal twice (0.382s per flash,
CSS overlay, rounded rect at 0.5 opacity, mix-blend-mode screen). Left
strip text changes to "LINK SENT" with a teal dot, pulsing 2.618s.
Dev helper (dev builds only, never in production): a small glass banner
under the card with the mock reset link "OPEN MOCK RESET LINK" pointing to
/reset-password?token=demo-valid. Label it DEV ONLY.
- Commit.

SLICE 3: /reset-password (new password screen)
Reads ?token=. mockAuth.verifyResetToken(token) returns "valid",
"expired" or "invalid". Rules in mockAuth.ts only:
 token "demo-valid" = valid, "demo-expired" = expired, anything else
 = invalid.
VALID state content:
- H1 "Set a new code."
- Sub "Choose a strong password for your vault."
- New password input (show/hide toggle, autocomplete="new-password").
- Confirm password input (autocomplete="new-password").
- Strength meter under the first input: five 13px bolts in a row joined by
  a 1px steel line. Each satisfied level slides a bolt shut: it fills brass
  with a 0.236s slide (x -5 to 0) and a soft glow. Level rules: 1 length
  >= 8, 2 lower and upper case, 3 a digit, 4 a symbol, 5 length >= 12.
  Mono label right of the bolts: WEAK / OK / GOOD / STRONG (levels 0-1,
  2, 3-4, 5). Label color: danger, brass text color, teal text color,
  success. Announce level changes via aria-live polite (debounced 0.618s).
- Requirements list (mono 12px) with check icons that turn success as
  met: "8+ characters", "Upper and lower case", "A number". Level 2 or
  higher is required to submit; the list shows exactly what is missing.
- Mismatch error under Confirm: "Passwords don't match." (on blur and on
  submit).
- Primary button "Set new password" (brass, 55px), disabled until valid.
- Left strip: "NEW CODE" with a steel dot.
Submit:
- Spinner 0.618s min. Success: keypad plays K1 to the last frame (code
  entry, green LED) using the existing keypad clip player. If the clip is
  not loaded, skip it and use the CSS fallback (green dot overlay at the
  keypad LED). The strip reads "CODE UPDATED" in the success color. The
  card cross-fades to the success state.
- Failure (mock 5% error): inline error and a card shake x +/-8px, 0.382s,
  keypad overlay flashes muted red once (0.382s). Strip reads "CODE
  REJECTED" for 1.618s.
SUCCESS state content:
- Success icon (shield with a check, draws in 0.618s).
- H1 "Vault re-secured."
- Body "Your password was updated. Sign in with your new password."
- Primary button "Sign in" (brass, 55px). Auto-redirect to /signin after
  2.618s with a 2px brass progress line under the button. Any key or click
  cancels the auto-redirect; the button remains.
EXPIRED and INVALID states:
- H1 "This link has expired." (or "This link isn't valid.")
- Body "Request a new reset link to continue."
- Primary button "Request a new link" going to /forgot-password.
- Strip reads "LINK EXPIRED" in danger text color.
- Keypad overlay flashes muted red once.
Entrance and transitions follow the same pattern as Slice 1.
- Commit.

- Change the "Forgot password?" href on /signin to /forgot-password

- Add the route entries in App.tsx for /forgot-password and

- Commit.

- Vault on top (38.2svh zone, as in the hero mobile layout). Card full

- Use 100svh and safe-area padding. The keyboard must not cover the primary

- Commit.

- Reduced motion: no entrance timeline, no shimmer, no shake, no bolt

  strength meter still updates.
- Status is never color alone. Text and icons accompany every state.

  4) token=demo-expired and token=foo show the right dead-end states.
  5) Resend: disabled for 55s, countdown visible, enabled afterwards.

  6) Same screen result for a registered and an unregistered email.
  7) Direct load of each route renders the final state. Browser back
     reverses the transition.
- The vault stays mounted across the three routes. Clips stay aligned.
- FX.forgotFlow = false: the link behaves as before.
- Keyboard-only run: complete the full flow with no mouse.
- Reduced motion verified. CLS 0.00. No overflow-x.
- Contrast table for chips, status text, buttons, and the strength labels.

DELIVERABLE
Commit list, files changed, measured values, the contrast table, any value

{"kind":"tool","id":"kJVyOrJVxRE","toolName":"str_replace","input":{"path":"src/lib/mockAuth.ts","replacements":[{"oldString":"/* the mock: "fail@" is always refused, anything else that validates is accepted.","newString":"/* ---- password reset (mock) ----
   Local only, like everything else in this file. Each function is named after the
   call it will make once the backend exists:

     requestReset(email)            -> POST /v1/auth/forgot-password
     verifyResetToken(token)        -> GET  /v1/auth/reset-password/validate
     resetPassword(token, password) -> POST /v1/auth/reset-password

   Nothing here says whether an address has an account: the request screen has to
   answer the same way either way. */

export const RESEND_SECONDS = 55;
export const RESET_LINK_MINUTES = 30;
/* the link the dev banner under the card opens */
export const MOCK_RESET_LINK = "/reset-password?token=demo-valid";

export const RESET_EMAIL_EMPTY = "Enter your email.";
export const RESET_EMAIL_BAD = "Enter a valid email address.";
export const RESET_SEND_ERROR = "Couldn't send. Try again.";
export const RESET_TOO_MANY = `Too many attempts. Try again in ${RESEND_SECONDS} seconds.`;
export const RESET_MISMATCH = "Passwords don't match.";
export const MAX_RESET_SENDS = 3;

/* the reset screen asks for the same address rule, with its own empty message */
export function resetEmailError(value: string): string | null {
  if (!value.trim()) return RESET_EMAIL_EMPTY;
  return EMAIL_RE.test(value.trim()) ? null : RESET_EMAIL_BAD;
}

/* how many requests this tab has made: three is the sandbox's limit */
let resetSends = 0;
export const resetSendCount = () => resetSends;
export const noteResetSend = () => (resetSends += 1);

/* the answer is always the same, and it never names an account */
export function requestReset(email: string): { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string } {
  /* the address is what the real call will send; nothing local reads it */
  void email;
  return { ok: true };
}

export type ResetTokenState = "valid" | "expired" | "invalid";

/* demo-valid and demo-expired are the two readable tokens; anything else is
   refused, including no token at all */
export function verifyResetToken(token: string | null): ResetTokenState {
  if (token === "demo-valid") return "valid";
  if (token === "demo-expired") return "expired";
  return "invalid";
}

export function resetPassword(
  token: string | null,
  password: string
): { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string } {
  const state = verifyResetToken(token);
  if (state !== "valid") {
    return { ok: false, error: state === "expired" ? "This link has expired." : "This link isn't valid." };
  }
  if (password.length < MIN_PASSWORD) {
    return { ok: false, error: `Use at least ${MIN_PASSWORD} characters.` };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"kJYzMVDVPmY","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/AuthField.tsx","instructions":"Field block (label, input, error) for the reset screens","content":"/* AuthField.tsx — label, input, error. The reset screens repeat this small block
   rather than sharing /signin's inline one (see the scope note); the classes are
   the same, so the two read as one card. A field with a trailing control (the
   show/hide toggle) gets the wrapper that reserves room for it. */

import { forwardRef } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

export interface AuthFieldProps {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  type: string;
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  onBlur?: () => void;
  onFocus?: () => void;
  /* the message under the field, already worded */
  error?: string | null;
  /* a submit failure is the only error a screen reader interrupts for */
  alert?: boolean;
  hint?: string;
  autoComplete?: string;
  inputMode?: "email" | "text";
  trailing?: ReactNode;
}

export const AuthField = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, AuthFieldProps>(function AuthField(
  {
    id,
    label,
    type,
    value,
    onChange,
    onBlur,
    onFocus,
    error,
    alert = false,
    hint,
    autoComplete,
    inputMode,
    trailing,
  },
  ref
) {
  const errorId = `${id}-err`;
  const hintId = `${id}-hint`;
  const describedBy = error ? errorId : hint ? hintId : undefined;

  return (
    <div className="signin-field">
      <label className="signin-label" htmlFor={id}>
        {label}
      </label>
      <div className={trailing ? "signin-pw" : undefined}>
        <input
          ref={ref}
          id={id}
          className="signin-input"
          type={type}
          name={id}
          value={value}
          onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)}
          onBlur={onBlur}
          onFocus={onFocus}
          autoComplete={autoComplete}
          inputMode={inputMode}
          spellCheck={false}
          aria-invalid={error ? true : undefined}
          aria-describedby={describedBy}
        />
        {trailing}
      </div>
      {hint && !error && (
        <p className="auth-hint" id={hintId}>
          {hint}
        </p>
      )}
      {error && (
        <p className="signin-err" id={errorId} role={alert ? "alert" : undefined} data-testid={`${id}-err`}>
          {error}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
});
"}}
{"kind":"tool","id":"kJZV8_HvXEg","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/PadFlash.tsx","instructions":"Keypad flash and LED overlays for the reset screens","content":"/* PadFlash.tsx — the vault's answers to the reset screens: the keypad hotspot
   flashing, and the lit LED when the clip cannot run.

   The keypad's own rect is measured from the live DOM each time, so a flash lands
   on the keypad whatever the viewport is doing, and it is drawn as an overlay
   rather than by touching the vault. Reduced motion gets nothing: every state
   these flashes announce is also written in the strip. */

import { forwardRef, useImperativeHandle, useRef } from "react";
import gsap from "gsap";

export interface PadFlashHandle {
  /* teal twice for a link sent, muted red once for a refusal */
  flash: (kind: "teal" | "red", times?: number) => void;
  /* the code-updated beat without the keypad clip: the LED lights green */
  led: () => void;
}

export interface PadFlashProps {
  reduced: boolean;
}

/* one flash, from nothing, up and back down */
const FLASH = 0.382;

export const PadFlash = forwardRef<PadFlashHandle, PadFlashProps>(function PadFlash({ reduced }, ref) {
  const tealRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const redRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const ledRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);

  const place = (el: HTMLElement | null, target: Element | null) => {
    if (!el || !target) return false;
    const r = target.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (!r.width || !r.height) return false;
    Object.assign(el.style, {
      left: `${r.left}px`,
      top: `${r.top}px`,
      width: `${r.width}px`,
      height: `${r.height}px`,
    });
    return true;
  };

  useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({
    flash(kind, times = 1) {
      if (reduced) return;
      const el = kind === "teal" ? tealRef.current : redRef.current;
      if (!place(el, document.querySelector(".hero-keypad"))) return;
      gsap.killTweensOf(el);
      const tl = gsap.timeline();
      for (let i = 0; i < times; i += 1) {
        tl.fromTo(el, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 0.5, duration: FLASH / 2, ease: "power2.out" }).to(
          el,
          { opacity: 0, duration: FLASH / 2, ease: "power2.in" }
        );
      }
    },
    led() {
      if (reduced) return;
      const led = ledRef.current;
      if (!place(led, document.querySelector(".hero-led"))) return;
      gsap.killTweensOf(led);
      gsap.fromTo(
        led,
        { opacity: 0 },
        { opacity: 1, duration: 0.236, ease: "power2.out", overwrite: "auto" }
      );
    },
  }));

  return (
    <div className="auth-pad" aria-hidden="true">
      <div className="auth-pad-teal" ref={tealRef} data-testid="pad-flash-teal" />
      <div className="auth-pad-red" ref={redRef} data-testid="pad-flash-red" />
      <div className="auth-pad-led" ref={ledRef} data-testid="pad-led" />
    </div>
  );
});
"}}


{"kind":"tool","id":"kJbD31oTl6w","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/StrengthMeter.tsx","instructions":"Five-bolt strength meter and the requirement list rules","content":"/* StrengthMeter.tsx — the five bolts and their label, plus the rules behind them.

   The rules are read straight off the spec: length, mixed case, a digit, a
   symbol, then the longer length. A level is how many of those the password
   satisfies, which is also what the two callers gate on (level 2 to submit). */

export type StrengthTone = "danger" | "brass" | "teal" | "success";

export interface Strength {
  /* 0..5, one per satisfied rule */
  level: number;
  label: "WEAK" | "OK" | "GOOD" | "STRONG";
  tone: StrengthTone;
  /* the three rules the requirements list names, plus the two the bolts show */
  rules: [boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean];
}

export const RULES = [
  "8+ characters",
  "Upper and lower case",
  "A number",
] as const;

export function strengthOf(password: string): Strength {
  const rules: [boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean] = [
    password.length >= 8,
    /[a-z]/.test(password) && /[A-Z]/.test(password),
    /[0-9]/.test(password),
    /[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test(password),
    password.length >= 12,
  ];
  const level = rules.filter(Boolean).length;
  const label: Strength["label"] = level <= 1 ? "WEAK" : level === 2 ? "OK" : level <= 4 ? "GOOD" : "STRONG";
  const tone: StrengthTone =
    level <= 1 ? "danger" : level === 2 ? "brass" : level <= 4 ? "teal" : "success";
  return { level, label, tone, rules };
}

export function StrengthMeter({ level, label, tone, rules }: Strength) {
  return (
    <div className="auth-meter">
      <div className="auth-bolts" aria-hidden="true">
        {rules.map((on, i) => (
          <span className="auth-bolt-track" key={i}>
            <span className="auth-bolt" data-on={on ? "1" : "0"} />
          </span>
        ))}
      </div>
      {/* the visible grade is repeated in the live region, so it is not read twice */}
      <span className="auth-grade" data-tone={tone} data-testid="strength-label" aria-hidden="true">
        {label}
      </span>
      <span className="sr-only" data-testid="strength-level">
        {`strength ${level} of 5`}
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

/* the list beside the field: what is missing, worded as the spec words it */
export function RequirementList({ strength }: { strength: Strength }) {
  const met = [strength.rules[0], strength.rules[1], strength.rules[2]];
  return (
    <ul className="auth-reqs">
      {RULES.map((text, i) => (
        <li className="auth-req" key={text} data-met={met[i] ? "1" : "0"}>
          <span className="auth-req-mark" aria-hidden="true">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
              strokeWidth="3" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
              <path d="M4 13l5 5L20 6" />
            </svg>
          </span>
          {text}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
"}}

{"kind":"tool","id":"kJfFUValx24","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/pages/auth/auth.css","instructions":"New stylesheet for the forgot/reset screens","content":"/* auth.css — what the reset screens add on top of /signin's sheet. The card, the
   fields, the strip, the wordmark and the brass primary are the classes from
   signin.css and hero.css; only what is genuinely new lives here: the status
   tones, the five-bolt meter, the keypad overlays, the drain lines and the dev
   banner.

   Text colours. Three of the token colours are too light to carry small text on
   this glass — success #1F9D6B lands at 2.97:1 and is used here for fills and
   rings only; the two given darker variants (#0A6A74 teal, #7A551A brass) and
   --failed (#9B1C16) carry the small text, with --auth-success-text the one
   value invented for this page so a met requirement clears 4.5:1. The ratios are
   in the report. */

:root {
  /* the smaller, darker success: 5.62:1 on the card's glass */
  --auth-success-text: #0f6b49;
}

/* the spec's card shadow (and the only line where these cards differ from

{"kind":"tool","id":"kLMmGu6d2mo","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"scripts/auth-contrast.mjs","instructions":"Measure the contrast ratios on the rendered reset screens","content":"/* auth-contrast.mjs — the ratios the reset screens actually render. The card is
   glass over a gradient, so the background is sampled from a screenshot rather
   than guessed: one pixel inside the card, one inside each button's fill. */

import { chromium } from "playwright";
import sharp from "sharp";

const base = process.env.BASE ?? "http://127.0.0.1:5173";

const lin = (c) => {
  const s = c / 255;
  return s <= 0.03928 ? s / 12.92 : ((s + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
};
const lum = ([r, g, b]) => 0.2126 * lin(r) + 0.7152 * lin(g) + 0.0722 * lin(b);
const ratio = (a, b) => {
  const [hi, lo] = [lum(a), lum(b)].sort((x, y) => y - x);
  return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05);
};
const hex = (h) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16));

const browser = await chromium.launch();
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  Math.random = () => 0.9;
});
await page.goto(`${base}/forgot-password`);
await page.waitForTimeout(900);

const at = async (x, y) => {
  const buf = await page.screenshot({ clip: { x: Math.round(x), y: Math.round(y), width: 1, height: 1 } });
  const { data } = await sharp(buf).raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
  return [data[0], data[1], data[2]];
};

const card = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const c = document.querySelector(".auth-card").getBoundingClientRect();
  const primary = document.querySelector('[data-testid="forgot-submit"]').getBoundingClientRect();
  return { c: { x: c.x, y: c.y, w: c.width, h: c.height }, p: { x: primary.x, y: primary.y, w: primary.width, h: primary.height } };
});

/* inside the card's padding, above the dev banner: glass, no text on it */
const cardBg = await at(card.c.x + card.c.w - 21, card.c.y + card.c.h - 120);
/* the primary button's fill at its darkest (the gradient runs light to dark) */
const brassBg = await at(card.p.x + card.p.w - 13, card.p.y + card.p.h - 8);

/* the glass secondary, from the sent state */
await page.locator("#forgot-email").fill("a@b.co");
await page.getByTestId("forgot-submit").click();
await page.getByTestId("forgot-sent").waitFor();
await page.waitForTimeout(600);
const glassRect = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const b = document.querySelector('[data-testid="sent-resend"]').getBoundingClientRect();
  return { x: b.x, y: b.y, w: b.width, h: b.height };
});
const glassBg = await at(glassRect.x + glassRect.w - 21, glassRect.y + glassRect.h - 8);

const rows = [
  ["ink #0E1520 on the card", hex("#0e1520"), cardBg],
  ["slate #4B5663 on the card", hex("#4b5663"), cardBg],
  ["teal text #0A6A74 on the card", hex("#0a6a74"), cardBg],
  ["brass text #7A551A on the card", hex("#7a551a"), cardBg],
  ["success text #0F6B49 on the card", hex("#0f6b49"), cardBg],
  ["danger text #9B1C16 on the card", hex("#9b1c16"), cardBg],
  ["ink on the brass fill", hex("#0e1520"), brassBg],
  ["ink on the glass fill", hex("#0e1520"), glassBg],
  ["steel #8A95A1 dot (graphic) on the card", hex("#8a95a1"), cardBg],
];

console.log(`card bg rgb(${cardBg.join(",")})  brass fill rgb(${brassBg.join(",")})  glass fill rgb(${glassBg.join(",")})`);
for (const [label, fg, bg] of rows) {
  console.log(`${ratio(fg, bg).toFixed(2)}:1\t${label}`);
}

await browser.close();
"}}

     requestReset(email)            -> POST /v1/auth/forgot-password
